status: advisory proposals, not a formal registered hypothesis set

candidates.question: Under physical-bearing and acquisition-session grouped splits, can a condition-aware representation improve diagnosis and calibration on unseen assets under equal CPU/tuning budgets?
rival_explanations: Split leakage or shared preprocessing explains the gain.
A transparent feature baseline already captures the effect.
candidates.falsification: Require multiple held-out assets and matched baselines; gains disappearing after grouped controls or calibration deterioration would refute the intended claim.

candidates.question: In an authorized small state-based simulation with explicit actuator/sensor degradation, can bounded offline-policy adaptation reduce violations while preserving task success under an equal interaction budget?
rival_explanations: Extra interactions or easier disturbances explain the gain.
The policy appears safe only because it stops or fails tasks.
candidates.falsification: Jointly assess held-out degradation, task success and constraints against fixed-policy and simple-controller baselines; no physical safety claim from simulation.

candidates.question: Can a fixed-compute industrial inspection system recognize unreliable decisions under held-out acquisition conditions while preserving prespecified coverage and small-defect sensitivity?
rival_explanations: Test-condition tuning or pretrained exposure explains apparent robustness.
Abstaining on nearly every difficult case hides failure.
candidates.falsification: Hold out acquisition groups before calibration; compare risk with coverage and defect sensitivity under matched budgets, without unsupported distribution-free guarantees.

limits: No numerical outcome, success threshold or effect size invented.
No paper or thesis allocation decided.
Every real experiment still requires the approved G3 plan, budget hashes and existing experiment runner.
